en.title: Marvel Drops 5 New Manga for Japan, Featuring Spider-Man & More
en.summary: Get ready for a new wave of Marvel in manga form. The publisher has partnered with Kadokawa to launch five original manga titles, bringing iconic heroes to Japanese audiences.
en.body:
Marvel and Japanese publisher **Kadokawa** are diving headfirst into the world of manga, announcing a significant partnership that will bring five original manga titles to life. This collaboration, aimed squarely at Japanese audiences, marks a major expansion of **Kadokawa**’s relationship with **Marvel** and promises to deliver fresh takes on some of the company’s most beloved characters.

The initial wave of this ambitious project includes manga centered around **Spider-Man** and **Spider-Gwen**. **Spider-Man of Shibuya** is set to swing onto **Kadokawa**’s KadoComi digital service before the end of 2026, offering a new urban adventure for the web-slinger. Following closely behind, **Spider-Gwen** will also debut on the platform within the same timeframe, giving fans a chance to explore the multiverse from a different perspective. The art for these titles, showcased at San Diego Comic-Con, has already generated considerable excitement, hinting at unique visual styles and storytelling approaches.

## A Universe of New Manga

Beyond the web-slinging heroes, the partnership extends to other fan-favorite characters. Concept art has also been revealed for manga featuring **Daredevil**, **The Punisher**, and **Deadpool**. While specific titles and creators for these three series are yet to be announced, the reveal has certainly piqued the interest of fans eager to see how these gritty and often irreverent characters will be translated into the manga medium. The initiative ties into **C.B. Cebulski**’s new **Marvel Asia Originals** role, underscoring **Marvel**’s dedication to fostering original content tailored for Asian markets. **Ryuusei Yamada** is attached to **Spider-Man of Shibuya**, and **Tokitokoro** is the artist for **Spider-Gwen**, bringing established manga talent into the fold.

## What This Means for Fans

This venture is more than just new comic books; it’s a deliberate effort to engage with a global fanbase on their own terms. By collaborating with **Kadokawa**, a titan in the Japanese publishing industry, **Marvel** is tapping into a rich storytelling tradition and a massive, passionate audience. For binge-watchers and series fans, this means a potential treasure trove of new narratives, character explorations, and artistic interpretations that could influence the broader **Marvel** Cinematic Universe and beyond. The focus on original stories for Japanese readers suggests a deep respect for cultural nuances and a desire to create content that resonates authentically, rather than simply adapting existing Western narratives.

## What's Next

With **Spider-Man of Shibuya** and **Spider-Gwen** slated for release by the end of 2026 on **Kadokawa**’s KadoComi platform, fans have a clear target to look forward to. Details on the **Daredevil**, **Punisher**, and **Deadpool** manga are expected to be rolled out gradually, so keep an eye on official announcements for further updates on creators, titles, and release windows.

content_raw: Manga about Iron Man, Spider-Man, Spider-Gwen, Deadpool, Venom launched on Sunday
